body: It was a serene place of worship having historical legends, surrounded by panoramic views of the Indian ocean, formed with gigantic rocks. body: The temple close to Tissamaharama and could be reached by traversing 7 km along the Tissamaharama – Kirinda road.It was as built by King Kawanthissa,the husband of Queen Viharamahadevi.According to the historical records and stories, some believe that Kirinda is the place where prince Viharamahadevi drifted ashore. King Kalanithissa, who rules Kalaniya was the father of prince Viharamahadevi. In second century BC, there was rising sea water level situation ( this may be the first Tsunami Situation recorded in Sri Lanka) occurred in Kalaniya. People thought that it’s due to the sin committed by the king Kalanithissa, by ordering to kill a monk. So to amend that sin, he was asked to sacrifice his daughter , princes Viharamahadevi by setting her ashore. After her landing to the Kirinda area, king kawanthissa, who ruled Ruhunu kingdom, welcomed her and later married her. They got two sons, prince Dutugamnu and prince Thissa.The temple sits on top of the rock with magnificent scenic views of Kirinda town, and as its back drop, vistas of beaches, sand dunes and the Indian Ocean. To reach its summit there are steps cut into rock and a recent addition of paved stairs.At its summit there are statues of Lord Buddha, Queen Viharamahadevi, a Stupa, the Devalaya, a Bo tree and its temple. Kirinda Rajamaha Viharaya is a place well worth visiting, an early morning or late evening visit would be comfortable to avoid the heat.
title: Kirinda Raja Maha Viharaya (Temple)

body: this the place as per the Sri lankan history where vihara maha devi landed....!Queen Viharamahadevi was the daughter of King Kelanitissa who ruled Kelaniya. The King once punished an innocent monk by boiling him alive in a cauldron of oil. It is said that the gods, angered over this cruel deed, made the ocean rush inland and flood the land. Soothsayers said that if a princess was sacrificed to the sea, the raging waves would stop. The young princess sacrificed herself for the sins of her father and for the safety of her motherland. body: Kirinda is a small town in Kataragama - Tissamaharama road about 10 km from Tissamaharama. Most of the people miss this beautiful place since this is little away from the main road. But I think this is a must visit place if you visit Kararagama and a place you can visit throughout the year.The ancient temple build in 2nd century BC attracts many pilgrims. There is a legend around this place on "Princess Vihara Maha Devi" who is the mother of "King Dutugemunu" a very famous king who saved his country, nation and the religion from its enemies. A magnificent view of the sea with its long stretch of beach can be seen on top of the rock. The sea at the bottom of the rock boulders is very rough though very beautiful. A huge statue of Buddha ( standing) is there on top the rock. And also a statue of Princess Viharamaha Devi too is there.

title: Culturally significant site with spectacular sea views
body: Kirinda temple sits on top of a rocky outcrop with a small 'Devalaya' adjacent to it. Legend has it that this is the place that Queen Vihara Maha Devi landed after being outcast at sea. Very little tourist infrastructure and certainly appears to be off the tourist trail but when we visited there were many local people praying at the temple which is apparently a place of pilgrimage. Rather than just be 'another temple' , there are spectacular views of the coast from the site which can extend to the Basses reef, one of Sri Lanka's premier dive sites. The temple is a bit out of the way but if you are in the Tissa Maha Rama area or near Bundula or Yala it is worth a visit.
